interpreter_matrix.note: paired medians vs same-window cp314hpo baseline (deployed: Arch python 3.14.7, CONFIG_ARGS '--without-lto', NO --enable-optimizations => no PGO, no LTO)
interpreter_matrix.verdict: INTERPRETER IS NOT THE LEVER: every version/build lands within +/-0.9% tok/s on all three workloads; python-outside-eval band 6.365-6.490 ms (+/-1.0%) with no monotone version or PGO effect. Even the exact native-macOS interpreter (3.11.16 PGO+LTO) shows 6.45 ms Python per token on Linux.

binding_cost_decomposition.microbench: eager per-op costs (ns/op, 2000 ops, (1,128) f32): ctor(x=x+1 lazy node) 31926-37867, eval(one-node) 322-476, pure-python dispatch loop 17.9-24.9
binding_cost_decomposition.reading: the Python-outside-eval term is ~99.9% C++ binding + array-node creation work (nanobind marshaling, mx::array allocation, graph wiring), not interpreter dispatch: pure-Python loop cost is 3 orders of magnitude below the per-op ctor cost, and ctor is invariant (within run noise) across interpreter version and PGO/LTO
binding_cost_decomposition.native_comparison: native macOS total token = 6.64 ms (150.57 tok/s) INCLUDING its C++ eval; Linux python-out alone = 6.4 ms. Swapping Linux onto the native interpreter environment (cp311pgo leg) moves nothing. The Linux-vs-native gap is therefore NOT interpreter artefact; it lives in the per-op binding/array-creation path and the backend eval share

wheel_flag_matrix.method: whole-lib LTO via CXXFLAGS/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS=-flto (verified: '-flto -O3 -DNDEBUG ...' in mlx.dir/flags.make); -mcpu=native via CXXFLAGS/CFLAGS (verified in flags.make); 5 paired reps each vs same-window cp314hpo, digests canonical on every leg
